newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two new bomb attacks in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Two new bomb attacks in Corsica.

text.p: Two new bomb attacks hit the troubled French Mediterranean island of Corsica overnight but no one was hurt, police said on Tuesday.

Both attacks were in the southern town of Bonifacio where one blast destroyed the parked car of the town's mayor, Doctor Ati Intieri, while the other damaged the door to a local restaurant, police said.
No one claimed responsibility for either attack.

The attacks came 24 hours after the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), "Historic Wing", the island's most hardline separatist group, claimed responsibility for a blast at the home of Emile Zuccarelli, a former cabinet minister and mayor of the north Corsican town of Bastia. He was not at home and no one was hurt.
In a statement to the media, the FLNC had also claimed responsibility for 17 other attacks since September 5, including the bombing of law courts, postal offices and banks.

The new wave of violence came after Francois Santoni, head of the Cuncolta Naziunalista party, legal facade of the FLNC, said in a newspaper interview that his group had held secret talks with the French government and he named five officials he called its envoys.
Santoni, who is living in hiding, said one of the envoys was Maurice Gourdault-Montagne, a senior aide of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
Juppe's office dismissed Santoni's statements as "grotesque lies by a terrorist."
Newspapers have said the centre-right government has had contact with the guerrillas to try to find a negotiated solution to end a 20-year low-level bombing campaign on the island.
